html:
The First Congo War, from 1996 to 1997, was an invasion of Zaire by Rwanda and Uganda, with a Congolese rebel front led by Laurent-Désiré Kabila, that overthrew Mobutu Sese Seko.

It grew from the refugee camps in eastern Zaire, where Hutu militias who had led the Rwandan genocide were rearming. Rwandan troops broke up the camps, killing many refugees, and then marched across the country with Kabila's forces, meeting little resistance from Mobutu's army.

Kinshasa fell in May 1997, Mobutu fled and died months later, and Kabila renamed the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo. His break with his backers led to the Second Congo War.
sum: The First Congo War, from 1996 to 1997, was an invasion of Zaire by Rwanda and Uganda, with a Congolese rebel front led by Laurent-Désiré Kabila, that overthrew Mobutu Sese Seko.
